items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: And I’m trying to think — Cozy Cole. Cozy was there. And just everybody who was anybody in jazz played in that place.

ctx.x: That’s amazing. How did they pay the musicians?

You’d go in and buy a beer. I’m not sure. They had a second story. They may have had an entrance fee because they put the bands up there. It may have cost you fifty cents or a dollar to get in. But you’d go there, and I’d just sit there and drink three or four bottles of beer in the night. Terrific. Marvelous. And as I say you stay at the bar and then as these people came off they’d swing by the bar and say hello and so on and so forth. And I’m trying to think — Cozy Cole. Cozy was there.
